Claude might not have improved my results directly.
Results still come down to execution, position size & sitting through the trade. What changed is speed. That matters more for me than most, because I do all this around a full-time job. 
Work that ate a weekend now fits into an evening.

Where I actually use it:

1. Chart Playbook database
Every setup I save gets logged with its context - pattern, ADR%, prior move, where it sat against the 11/21 EMA, what happened next. Claude keeps it structured & searchable, so I can pull up every NR7 near a 52-week high I've ever marked instead of scrolling through a folder of screenshots.

2. Obsidian + Claude Code
My second brain. Transcripts, strategy notes, setups & catalyst logs all go in, searchable & cross-linked. Everything below pulls from this.

3. Backtesting
Pine Script systems across NSE & NASDAQ. Parameter studies, pre-breakout fingerprints, plus the exit-rule test I still owe myself. This is probably best usage considering as I have no background of Coding 

4. Research
Concall analysis in a fixed format. Single-company deep dives. One running thread per name, revisited each quarter. Balance sheet template. Sometimes ranking a shortlist.

5. Dashboards
Core/Satellite portfolio. Market breadth - Stockbee-style, tuned to NSE. Python + Kite Connect + GitHub Actions.

6. TradingView
MCP link for quant studies off the charts, plus Pine Screener.

7. Journal review
TradesViz exports read against my edge. Hold time, R-multiples, which setup paid, whether I followed the plan. This produced my current 4-rule protocol.

8. Earnings calendar
Watchlist dates tracked, so nothing I hold surprises me.

9. Cowork
Monthly journal review or a 4-quarter concall batch, start to finish, while I'm at work.

10. YouTube content
Scripts, articles, posts, thumbnails, chart animations.

Edge is mine. Claude just removes everything standing between me & running it.

Want to Know If the Market Is Topping or Just Resetting for the Next Leg Higher? Read this.

Stan Weinstein’s framework gives us one of the simplest ways to answer it.

The Nasdaq ran 34% from the March low to the June high.

Then it spent three months going nowhere.The key is the 30-week moving average.

Stage 2 pause:
- 30-week MA still rising
- Price holds above it, pullbacks find support near the line
- Down weeks come on lighter volume
- The range eventually resolves higher

Stage 3 top:
- 30-week MA flattens out
- Price whips above and below the line
- Heavy volume shows up on down weeks
- Rallies keep failing at the same level

Right now, $QQQ sits above a 30-week line that is still rising.

By Weinstein’s framework, that looks more like a Stage 2 pause than a Stage 3 top.

That can change. The line flattening is the tell.

Until it does, the trend gets the benefit of the doubt.

Sideways above a rising line = pause.
Sideways through a flat line = potential top.

The market doesn’t need to go up every week to remain in an uptrend.

Sometimes the strongest moves come after months of doing nothing. We’ve seen this again and again - October 2023, April 2025, November 2025, and March 2026 are some of the best examples.

Until the 30-week MA tells us otherwise, the primary trend remains intact.

What are you in a hurry to prove this week?

That you can meet your weekly profit goal by Wednesday? That last month’s size is still the right size even though the action is more challenging? That sitting it out means you are falling behind your competition? 

I have felt all of that in my early years, usually on a weekend, when the year suddenly feels like it is running away from me and the only fix is to press something NOW

Rushing size after a good stretch, rushing a make-back after a sloppy one, rushing a week that was never offering you much: those are different costumes on the same itch. The market does not owe you a complete allocation just because the calendar is moving

The traders who last are not the ones who extract a result from every session. They are the ones who can leave a week disappointed but still be the same level-headed person on Monday. 

There is no rush. Don't be in a hurry to prove something. You have years to do this.

How trading saved my life 

I rarely talk about myself or my story, because I think it’s largely irrelevant. But as TSF grows, as I get to know more members and people, its only right to share a little about myself.

My name is Jonas, I’m an M.D, my biggest passion in life is my job. I work as a pediatric and neonatal intensive care physician and anesthesiologist. In short I take care of newborn babies and children that are critically ill. I have two little girls myself, I’m middle aged and my second passion in life is trading.

And trading saved my life. Because TSF didn’t start by chance, it started because I needed to be saved from what I was going through.

I have been trading for more than a decade, if you are part of TSF you know that I can read charts like I think few can, but I never had a real space where I could share my thoughts and observations.

But still, TSF didn’t start because I love trading, it started because I needed to immerse myself into something, to be able to distract myself from my current situation. 

Because I lost both of my parents almost at the same time, both were completely healthy and suddenly poff they were gone. When that happens to a young guy that just became a dad, it’s not an easy thing to handle.

So I did what I have been trained to do for years in med school, focus on something you can study, build and fixate about. And that’s how TSF started, it started from zero. And I mean zero.

And here we are about 1.5 years later, TSF is one of the largest trading communities on substack, 450+ members. And TSF and the people of TSF bring me joy daily, I am honored to be a part of TSF and share what I can to make us all better each day.

Which brings us to the last piece of this long ass tweet. Don’t do what I did and fixate about the market too much, that is not the way. It always costs something on the other end. 

Balance is key, if I have learned anything during the last couple of years, it’s that you will be a 10x better trader with clarity of mind. 

Lite is more than charts and money, enjoy it as long as it lasts

I landed here yesterday and have already learned WAY more than I expected, so I’m excited to share some of those lessons when I’m back.

A lot to reflect on, but even more to be thankful for.

📌 Today's Highlights — Friday, September 11
August CPI landed at 0.4% on the month and 3.4% year over year, in line, but core came in at 0.3% against the 0.2% expected and held 2.4% annual. "A rate hike next week is all but assured," one strategist put it.

Server makers repriced on someone else's guidance. Oracle's CFO put full-year capex at $90B to $95B, aimed at racks, cooling, power and networking gear, and $HPE rose 12%, $DELL 11% and $SMCI 7% — none of them with an announcement of their own. Super Micro's smaller move reflected the $60B order book it had already flagged Thursday night.

The consumer read went the other way. Preliminary September Michigan sentiment fell to 47.8 against 51.0 expected, the expectations component to 45.8, and year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6% from 4.0%. Futures odds on a hike Wednesday moved to 82% by the close.
